quotes.text: Most people think hallucination is a model problem, but the timelines revealed an architecture problem. A single agent blends retrieval and generation, making it impossible to test each stage
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes hallucinations as an architecture issue rather than a model flaw.

quotes.text: Retrieval stops pretending to reason. Generation stops pretending to verify. Verification stops pretending to retrieve.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Crisp statement of separation of duties between agents.

quotes.text: Everything changes when graph becomes the gate, not the suggestion. Permission aware retrieval must query Microsoft search or the Copilot retrieval API with the user's token, returning only authorized candidates.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Concrete rule against data leakage through over-broad indexes.

quotes.text: Audit failures don't happen in audits. They happen in design. If logging is optional, provenance is decorative and deployment variance is invisible, you've built a story generator, not a system of record.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Argues that auditability must be designed in from the start.

chapters.title: A confident answer with no chain of custody

takeaways: Single all-purpose agents hallucinate under token pressure and weak retrieval, so split retrieval, reranking, generation and verification into separate roles.
Permission-aware retrieval with the user's token, Purview labels as filters and red team and policy agents prevent context leakage through prompts and over-broad indexes.
Route every call through Azure API Management with correlation IDs and persisted retrieval sets so a compliance agent can re-enact any answer for audits.
hook: A single Copilot agent can invent evidence, leak restricted content and drift on stale indexes without anyone noticing. This episode gives architects and security teams a multi-agent reference architecture for Microsoft 365 and Azure OpenAI with a threat model and build steps that make every answer verifiable and auditable.
